Agreed. Maier stays parked as a same-shop comparator. I’m keeping the active question to one exposed variable:

$$
\boxed{\delta(e_{\rm return})=1}
$$

The immediate job is to determine whether the 1617 Fludd sequence and the 1619 Kepler sequence support “excursion first, level change on return,” or only supply ingredients compatible with it. Then we either justify the voltage placement, revise it, or leave it explicitly stipulated and resume unit alignment.

I’m staying on the one exposed variable: whether the first-edition Fludd–Kepler evidence actually licenses $\delta(e_{\rm return})=1$. I’m locating Kepler’s original 1619 MI–FA–MI passage and his exact comma/semitone definitions, then I’ll compare only those passages with Fludd’s 1617 solar-boundary sequence.

Kepler’s first edition has now supplied the exact missing arithmetic, in his own text: Book III defines the comma as $80{:}81$ and says subtracting it from the $15{:}16$ semitone leaves the Platonic limma $243{:}256$. In frequency orientation, that is precisely your inverse relation
$$
\frac{256}{243}\cdot\frac{81}{80}=\frac{16}{15}.
$$
I’m now checking the page images and the later Earth MI–FA–MI wording, because the critical question is whether Kepler also supplies the ordered motion, while Fludd supplies the register landing.

Yes. We have filled the gap as far as the surviving first-edition evidence presently permits, and we should return to SUN testing.

The result is stronger than “Fludd and Kepler contain compatible symbolism,” but narrower than “they explicitly published your complete boundary operator.”

What the first editions establish

1. Kepler supplies the exact comma correction

In Harmonices Mundi, Book III, page 39, Kepler defines the comma as $80{:}81$ in his string-length convention. He then states that removing this comma from the $15{:}16$ semitone leaves the Platonic limma $243{:}256$.

Converted to your frequency-ratio orientation:

$$
\boxed{
\frac{256}{243}\frac{81}{80}=\frac{16}{15}
}
$$

Therefore your correction

$$
\lambda=\frac{256}{243}
\quad\xrightarrow{\times,\kappa}\quad
\rho=\frac{16}{15},
\qquad
\kappa=\frac{81}{80},
$$

is not a modern numerical coincidence. It is the exact inverse of a relationship Kepler explicitly records in the 1619 first edition.

Kepler, Harmonices Mundi, first edition, Book III, p. 39

2. Kepler supplies the closed, direction-changing path

Book III explains that MI–FA or FA–MI always denotes the semitone. More decisively, Book V, page 207 prints in its margin:

Tellus canit vero MI FA MI...

Earth “sings MI–FA–MI.” The associated text says Earth’s motions vertuntur within the semitone: they turn or reverse there.

That gives us an attested ordered excursion:

$$
\boxed{
\mathrm{MI}\rightarrow\mathrm{FA}\rightarrow\mathrm{MI}
}
$$

It is a return path, rather than three unrelated pitch labels.

Kepler, Harmonices Mundi, first edition, Book V, p. 207

3. Fludd supplies the typed boundary

Fludd’s 1617 text places two minor-semitone regions around the solar intersection:

the lower solar portion participates in the material fifth;

the upper solar portion participates in the formal fifth;

ordinary generation receives its force from the lower region;

regeneration originates from the upper region and proceeds toward spiritual elevation.

He explicitly marks this location as one where, to a careful reader, a “divine mystery” reveals itself.

This means the two sides of the boundary are not interchangeable copies. They possess different types:

$$
\boxed{
\text{lower/material/generation}
\longrightarrow
\text{solar boundary}
\longrightarrow
\text{upper/formal/regeneration}
}
$$

Fludd, Utriusque Cosmi, first edition, p. 87

4. Fludd supplies the octave landing at that center

On the following page, Fludd says:

the complete world semidiameter has the quadruple proportion, a double octave;

a monochord pressed at its middle sounds an octave from the midpoint to either extremity;

a duplex harmonia Diapason is produced at the solar center;

the material and formal octaves correspond through that center.

Thus the center separating the lower and upper regions is simultaneously an octave/register junction.

Fludd, Utriusque Cosmi, first edition, p. 88

The reconstructed bridge

These first editions jointly provide four independently attested components:

Component
First-edition support
Status
Limma corrected by $81/80$ to $16/15$
Kepler, Book III p. 39
Explicit and exact
MI–FA–MI return motion
Kepler, Book V p. 207
Explicit
Different states on opposing sides of the boundary
Fludd p. 87
Explicit
Octave/register division at the boundary
Fludd p. 88
Explicit
MI return lands specifically on Fludd’s opposite octave sheet
Combined reconstruction
Inference

The clean reconstruction is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fludd limma}
&\xrightarrow{\times,81/80}
\text{Kepler semitone}\
&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{MI}\rightarrow\mathrm{FA}\rightarrow\mathrm{MI}}
\text{same local identity}\
&\xrightarrow{\text{crossing Fludd's typed solar center}}
\text{corresponding state in the next octave/register}.
\end{aligned}
}
$$

Formally:

$$
e_{\rm out}:
(\mathrm{MI},k)
\xrightarrow{(16/15,0)}
(\mathrm{FA},k),
$$

$$
e_{\rm return}:
(\mathrm{FA},k)
\xrightarrow{(15/16,1)}
(\mathrm{MI},k+1).
$$

Therefore:

$$
\boxed{
\gamma_{FK}
\mapsto
\left(\frac{16}{15},0\right)
\left(\frac{15}{16},1\right)
=(1,1)
}
$$

and:

$$
\boxed{
\Phi(1,1)=2^{-1}=\frac12.
}
$$

At Yesod:

$$
\boxed{
\frac F8
\rightarrow
\frac{2F}{15}
\rightarrow
\frac F{16}.
}
$$

The exact evidentiary limit

The first editions do not explicitly write

$$
\delta(e_{\rm return})=1.
$$

Neither author says, in one sentence, that completing Kepler’s MI–FA–MI motion changes the Fluddian octave register. That identification is your reconstruction.

But it is no longer an unconstrained invention. Each necessary part is independently present:

$$
\boxed{
\text{exact correction}
+
\text{returning motion}
+
\text{typed boundary}
+
\text{octave landing}.
}
$$

The remaining inference is their composition:

$$
\boxed{
\text{Kepler's returned MI}
\equiv
\text{Fludd's same identity across the formal/material octave boundary}.
}
$$

That is now the single falsifiable claim.

One historical precaution

Fludd’s “two commas” on page 87 should not yet be identified numerically with two syntonic commas $81/80$. In his Pythagorean framework, “major semitone minus minor semitone” can indicate the Pythagorean comma:

$$
\frac{2187/2048}{256/243}

\frac{531441}{524288}.
$$

Kepler’s $81/80$ relationship is explicit and exact. Fludd’s two commas establish a balanced discrepancy around the solar boundary, but their exact species remains separate unless Fludd defines it elsewhere.

Frozen SUN boundary

I would freeze the boundary with its evidence attached directly:

$$
\boxed{
B_{FK}=(Q_{FK},r,\delta,\Phi;\mathcal E)
}
$$

where:

$$
r(e_{\rm out})=\frac{16}{15},
\qquad
\delta(e_{\rm out})=0,
$$

$$
r(e_{\rm return})=\frac{15}{16},
\qquad
\delta(e_{\rm return})=1,
$$

and:

$$
\mathcal E=
\begin{cases}
r,\ \mathrm{MI!-!FA!-!MI} &: \text{Kepler-explicit},\
\text{typed boundary and octave} &: \text{Fludd-explicit},\
\delta(e_{\rm return})=1 &: \text{frozen assembly hypothesis}.
\end{cases}
$$

That is scientifically clean. It prevents the historical evidence, mathematical proof, and your synthesis from being blurred together.

The boundary is sufficiently constrained to resume the correspondence matrix. The next tests should evaluate whether $\delta=1$ predicts the intermediate order, subunits, functions, and downstream generative behavior of aligned units better than the controls $\delta=0$ and premature lift $(1,0)$. That evidence can now decide the one thing the surviving texts do not explicitly decide for us.
